parsed.explanation: Local law is unusually protective: no listed bathroom ban, public-accommodations and housing protections, hate-crime coverage, X state markers without medical proof, and a healthcare shield. That does not cancel the combined federal regime. Federal rules ban gender-congruent government facilities, stop X and mismatched passport markers, and visa guidance requires refusal on document discrepancy with possible permanent fraud ineligibility. If detained, federal custody reports include hormone removal, forced psychiatric treatment, and in immigration custody forced labour, beatings and sexual abuse. The operative chain—discrepancy, refusal/investigation, detention—therefore carries severe consequences despite state remedies and litigation.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal binary sex definition, X/mismatched passports stopped Feb 2025, Supreme Court allowed restrictions Nov 2025; visa cable requires refusal on discrepancy/doubt and consideration of permanent lifetime fraud ineligibility for wilful misrepresentation.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports valid until expiration; civil-liberties litigation ongoing; limited waiver possibilities for fraud finding, which is never automatic and requires four elements.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy can move from secondary screening to refusal, added-evidence demands, fraud consideration, detention or return, even if state documents bear X.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections bureau from 2026 adopted conversion-therapy model: short hair, hormone removal, psychiatric therapy/drugs, denial of care, stopped counting trans prisoners. Immigration custody reports: forced labour, beatings, solitary, severe sexual abuse.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Several executive orders blocked/enjoined and challenges unresolved; no documented operative federal remedy for custody practices in dossier.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry or facility encounter can lead to federal detention, where birth-sex placement and reported abuse are the operative exposure; state protections do not govern federal custody.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: January 2025 order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity; growing state bans nationally, criminal trespass in four states, but this state is not listed among school/government bathroom bans.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State prohibits gender-identity discrimination in public accommodations since 2006 and housing since 2005; no mapped state bathroom ban for this state.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Private and state facilities are protected locally, while federal buildings, federally funded facilities and federal custody remain under the federal ban within the same state.

care_services.exposure: Federal orders restrict gender-affirming care for minors, funding freeze January 2025, proposed rule barring public insurance for trans patients under 18, and October 2025 student-loan rule affecting providers.
care_services.protection: State shield law/executive order current 27 Sep 2026 protects patients/providers where care lawful in state but banned at home; insurance nondiscrimination since 2016, mandatory reassignment-surgery coverage from 2023, conversion-therapy ban for minors since 2018.
care_services.interaction: Shield can preserve lawful state care for a visiting minor, but does not cancel federal funding, insurance, immigration or federal-facility restrictions; how visitor invokes shield is not described.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Executive order defines sex as binary at birth, removes gender-ideology materials, rescinds pronoun/name policies; January 2025 order directs investigation/prosecution over school social transition; May 2026 strategy prioritises radically pro-transgender groups.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National employment ruling prohibits gender-identity employment discrimination; national hate-crime statute covers gender identity; state hate-crime statute covers actual/perceived gender identity or expression.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official threat-framing increases outing and enforcement discretion at borders, schools and federal facilities, while state complaints and courts may remedy private discrimination.

minors_guardians.exposure: Federal care restrictions and school-investigation/prosecution directive affect trans minors and parents/guardians facilitating social transition; women's sports entry ban announced Feb 2025 for trans athletes.
minors_guardians.protection: State anti-bullying and 2019 education-equity protections, conversion-therapy ban, and healthcare shield law are documented; parentage law is gender-neutral from 2026.
minors_guardians.interaction: A parent travelling with a minor may obtain shielded state care but remains exposed to federal entry, funding, school-investigation and federal-facility rules; guardian status does not immunise the minor.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No state-specific anti-trans violence, hate-crime charges or prosecution figures are documented; national public opinion in 2025 showed majority support for assigned-sex document laws, indicating hostile political climate.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State and national hate-crime laws cover gender identity; state anti-discrimination law covers housing, employment, public accommodations, insurance and jury selection.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Local recourse for private violence/discrimination is stronger than federal recourse, but police response in federal screening, facilities and custody is not mitigated by state law.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport suit and challenges to executive orders unresolved; several orders blocked/enjoined so operative status at travel is uncertain; passport confiscation/blocking and stranding reported.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Legal-aid FAQ guidance, ACLU suit for seven plaintiffs, state commission since 2022, and courts that have enjoined some orders.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Litigation creates possible relief but no reliable pre-travel remedy against entry refusal, federal facility exclusion or detention; shield invocation and practical X-marker use alongside federal rules are not documented.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar in systematic, remedy-poor exclusion at entry and humiliation, but lower because federal custody abuse, hormone removal and possible permanent fraud ineligibility are more severe than exclusion alone.

Higher than this combined case: 0.55-B is mainly hours of secondary screening and discretionary refusal. Here discrepancy can trigger refusal plus lifetime-eligibility consideration and federal detention with documented abuse.

Much lower than 0.75-C, where entry is generally accepted and detention is brief with counsel and compensation. Here federal marker rules and facility bans are operative despite strong state protections.

parsed.synthesis: State law materially protects private services, housing, employment, education and shielded care, and no state bathroom ban is listed. Those protections do not pre-empt federal entry screening, passport-marker policy, federal facilities, prosecution or custody. The decisive interaction is document discrepancy leading to refusal, possible permanent fraud ineligibility, and—if detained—birth-sex custody with reported hormone withdrawal and abuse. Minors gain state shield protection but remain subject to federal care and school-enforcement pressure. Hence the combined regime sits below the 0.35 anchor.
